learn.pageTitle: How to Count Han from Yaku in Riichi Mahjong
learn.pageDescription: Han is the total of the yaku in a winning hand. Learn what yaku do and how closed and open hands (kuisagari) change their han, so you can count han correctly.
learn.whatIsYakuBody1: Han is determined by the [[yaku|yaku]] the hand has when you [[hora|win]] and the number of [[dora|dora]] in your [[tehai|hand]].
learn.whatIsYakuBody2: Dora are easy: you just count them.
learn.whatIsYakuBody3:
Yaku, on the other hand, require you to judge whether each one is complete.
Some yaku change their han depending on whether you have made [[furo|calls]], and it is common for several yaku to combine in one hand.
For these reasons, it takes some practice before you can reliably count the han of the yaku in a hand.
learn.menzenNakiBody1:
Some yaku no longer count once you call ([[pon|pon]], [[chii|chii]] or [[minkan|open kan]]).
For example, Riichi, [[pinfu|Pinfu]], Iipeikou and [[chiitoitsu|Chiitoitsu]] only count in a [[menzen|closed hand]].
learn.menzenNakiBody2:
Other yaku still count after you call, but are worth less.
This is generally called "[[kuisagari|kuisagari]]" (reduced when open).
learn.menzenNakiBody3:
For example, Sanshoku Doujun, Ittsu, Honitsu and Chinitsu all have this kuisagari property.
A kuisagari yaku is worth 1 han less when open than when closed.
learn.menzenNakiBody4: Some yaku, on the other hand, such as Tanyao and Toitoi, keep the same han even when open.
